I am 62 years old and have farmed these fields in Quzhou for 40 years. My land is 16.1 mu, and with only my wife and me at home now, I have to be smart about labor. I know this soil like the back of my hand, and I have well water I can count on.

I will put 10 mu into my wheat-maize double cropping system because that is the backbone of my farm — it gives me grain security and steady income. The remaining 6.1 mu I will plant with cotton. Cotton brings good money, but it is heavy work, especially the spraying. At my age, I cannot manage too much of it, but 6.1 mu is just right for the two of us to handle.

For the winter wheat, I will use an improved variety like the ones I have used before. I will do rotary tillage before sowing and apply my fertilizer with care: about 16 kg of nitrogen per mu, 6 kg of phosphorus, and 4 kg of potassium. I have learned over the years that more fertilizer does not always mean more grain, but balance does. I will irrigate three times — once before winter to protect the seedlings, once at jointing, and once at grain filling. I expect about 1,000 kg per mu if the weather cooperates.

For the summer maize, timing is everything after the wheat comes off in June. I will use a hybrid variety and plant with no-tillage to save time and keep moisture. I will put down 16 kg nitrogen, 4 kg phosphorus, and 5 kg potassium per mu, and irrigate twice — the rainy season usually helps, but I will water at the jointing stage and again at grain filling if it turns dry. I expect around 1,100 kg per mu. I will spray two or three times for weeds and pests.

For cotton, I will rotary till in spring and plant an improved variety. Cotton needs more potassium, so I will apply 14 kg nitrogen, 6 kg phosphorus, and 9 kg potassium per mu. I will irrigate three times during the key growing stages. I know cotton bollworm and aphids will come, so I will spray about 14 times through the season — it is a lot of work, but I have the experience to stay on top of it. I expect about 550 kg of seed cotton per mu.
